reason: The parenthetical is internally at odds with itself and with the envelope it defends: it labels the whole ~30 GB as 'activations' while its own first term is 'K+V alone ... ~= 24 GB' (KV cache, not activations), then characterises the ~30 GB as 'a transient single-request prefill peak, reused across the batch rather than held per request in flight'. That is false for the 24 GB KV component -- KV is exactly what IS held per request in flight, and at concurrency it is the quantity the 436 GB budget holds (17 x 24.9 ~= 423 GB ~= the 436 GB line). Only the ~6 GB of hidden/MLP working tensors is transient and drawn from the 64 GB workspace. The envelope 140 + 436 + 64 = 640 does close, but the reason the text gives for it (the whole 30 GB is transient/batch-reused) is wrong, so a reader cannot tell which envelope line each component belongs to -- the double-count risk the finding describes is real at the level of the stated reasoning.
evidence: chapter-25.md line 140 quote located verbatim: 'plus ~30 GB activations at the peak for this worked example (K+V alone: 2 x 80 layers x 9.2K x 8,192 x 2 B ~= 24 GB, plus hidden/MLP working tensors ~= 30 GB total) [DERIVED] ... the ~30 GB is a transient single-request prefill peak, reused across the batch rather than held per request in flight (17 concurrent x 30 GB is not implied) -- so the envelope closes as 140 + 436 + 64 = 640, not 670.'; python: 2*80*9200*8192*2 = 24.24e9 = 24.2 GB; 17*24.9 = 423.3 GB vs the 436 GB KV budget; 30 - 24.2 = 5.8 GB transient.
fix_instruction: design/manuscript/chapter-25/chapter-25.md, Sec4 derived quantity 1 (line 140): split the parenthetical into two lines -- 'per-request KV at 9.2K = 24.2 GB (2 x 80 layers x 9.2K x 8,192 x 2 B): KV, already inside the ~436 GB KV budget at concurrency (17 x ~24.9 GB ~= 423 GB)' and 'transient activation/workspace ~= 6 GB (hidden/MLP working tensors -- inside the 64 GB runtime/workspace reserve)' -- rename the headline '~30 GB activations' to '~30 GB KV + workspace (single-request working set)', restrict 'transient ... reused across the batch' to the ~6 GB component, and state that the ADR's single-request 170 GB footprint is not an envelope term.
